Decorative

/DEK-uh-ruh-tiv/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Decorative means attractive or ornamental in appearance; added to make something look nicer, often without any practical function

The bakery's window display featured a decorative tower of cupcakes that no one was actually allowed to buy.

Worked Example

The hotel lobby's grand staircase featured a decorative wrought-iron railing so intricately scrolled that guests routinely stopped to photograph it, even though a plain, code-compliant handrail ran alongside it for anyone who actually needed to hold on.

The scrolled railing exists to be admired, while a separate plain rail handles the actual safety function — a clean example of "decorative" describing something valued for appearance rather than use.

How Decorative Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

ornamental

ornamental: this unit's own related word, taught earlier — near-identical in meaning, though often used in more formal design/architecture contexts

embellishing

embellishing: emphasizes actively adding extra decorative detail to something

attractive

attractive: a broader, more general word for pleasing appearance

Antonyms

functional

functional: designed to serve a practical purpose rather than to look nice

plain

plain: simple and undecorated

How Strong Is It? — attractive → decorative → embellishing

attractive vs. decorative

attractive vs. decorative: Something attractive is simply pleasant to look at, without necessarily being extra or added-on.

embellishing vs. decorative

embellishing vs. decorative: Something embellishing actively adds extra decorative flourishes beyond the basic design.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of decorative.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — decor-

Root — decor-: beauty, ornament — the same root as decorate, taught earlier in this unit

Suffix — -at-

Suffix — -at-: the participial link carried over from decorate (Latin decoratus, 'adorned')

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: tending toward, having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Decor- (beauty, ornament — the same root as decorate, taught earlier) + -at- (the participial link carried over from decorate) + -ive (tending toward): while "decorate" is the action of adding beauty, "decorative" describes anything that already has that beautifying quality.

Use the root in a new word: decorous

Use the root in a new word: decorous: Even the toddlers at the formal wedding managed to stay remarkably decorous throughout the ceremony.
